title: Deployment telemetry mismatch investigation and auto-rollback policy proposals
creator: Asha Patel
description: Post-incident ticket to capture findings from the 2026-02-18 canary degradation where user-facing latency and hallucination signals diverged from shadow telemetry. Goal: close gaps in metric contracts, author a compact runbook for signal-led auto-rollback, and propose instrumentation changes so future rollouts trigger deterministic safety actions rather than manual triage.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha Patel: Initial triage notes: 02/18 canary at 10% produced a 3.2x increase in tail latency for long-context requests and a correlated uptick in hallucination score on production prompts. Shadow traffic metrics did not show the same latency spike — hypothesis: sampling bias + KV-cache warmup behavior produced a telemetry mismatch.

2026-02-20 - Marco Ruiz: Reproduced increased p99 on a dedicated perf harness when synthetic long-sequence prompts (>=2048 tokens) were replayed with the same model variant — indicates kernel scheduling regressions under streaming + long-context workload.

2026-02-22 - Lina Gomez (SRE): Observed that shadow traffic pipeline samples 95th-percentile requests but strips streaming tokens and uses smaller default batch sizes; these differences likely hid the degradation. Added shadow sampling variance to investigation scope.
2026-02-25 - PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 - perf: adjust kernel scheduler heuristics when streaming + seq_len>1024. Marked as draft until rollout gating updated.

2026-03-01 - Product review (Jon Miller): Agreed that auto-rollback triggers should rely on multiple orthogonal signals (latency p99, hallucination regression on golden prompts, error-rate, and kv-cache miss-rate) with a configurable hysteresis window. Asked eng to propose a minimal policy we can pilot in Dedicated clusters.

2026-03-05 - Design feedback (Maya Chen): Console UX needs an explicit telemetry contract page for each rollout to avoid silent mismatches in sampling/aggregation. Will prototype a telemetry diff view in Console-2026.04.

2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz: Added synthetic replay harness results to the ticket attachments. Replay showed model variant A->B transition increases async queueing under sustained 50qps long-context load. Candidate mitigation: reduce max-continuous-batch-window for streaming workloads or add a streaming-aware kernel path.
2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Draft auto-rollback policy posted for review. Seeking feedback from SRE and Product by 2026-03-16 so we can land the policy before release-2026.03 cut.

2026-03-12 - Lina Gomez: Question — what’s the expected false positive rate if we use KV-cache miss-rate as an input? We should quantify with at least 3 weeks of historical telemetry before enabling on hosted tier.
decisions: Use a multi-signal rollback policy that requires 2 out of 4 signals to breach thresholds within a 10-minute sliding window before initiating auto-rollback
Signals to evaluate: latency_p99 (production), golden_prompt_quality_drop (regression on control prompts), kv_cache_miss_rate, request_error_rate (5xx/timeout)

Shadow pipeline sampling must match production sampling for key dimensions: streaming enabled, sequence_length bucketing, and client-level sampling distribution. Modify shadow sampling to include explicit long-context and streaming buckets.
Pilot auto-rollback in Dedicated clusters only for the first iteration; disable on free hosted tiers until we establish acceptable false positive / false negative rates.
Add a 'telemetry contract' artifact to the rollout configuration UI that surfaces sampling, aggregation windows, and which signals will be used for gating/rollback.
Require a canary 'warmup' stage: small synthetic replay for 5 minutes to exercise KV-cache and kernel scheduling before opening canary to live clients.
